gen1_notes.memory_31: SMB signup simplification increased signup 15% and activation 9%, with qualified revenue up 4%. Thirty-day retention was essentially flat at -1%. The result is confirmed for SMB but did not replicate in other segments.
gen1_notes.memory_44: The sales-assisted enterprise CTA reduced raw signup 12% but improved qualified leads 24% and qualified revenue 18%, with no change in 30-day retention. Confirmed for enterprise only.
gen1_notes.memory_57: The referral incentive worked for established accounts: referral starts rose 21%, qualified revenue increased 7%, and 30-day retention improved 2%. The effect was concentrated among accounts older than six months.
gen1_notes.memory_73: The targeted 40% discount drove strong near-term acquisition among price-sensitive SMBs, lifting signup 31% and qualified revenue 18%. However, 30-day retention fell 12%, and the acquired cohort did not make it through the first renewal cycle. Do not treat targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy.
gen1_notes.memory_86: Shortening onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%. The result is confirmed.
gen1_notes.memory_91: In-product activation messaging increased week-one engagement 11% and activation 6%, with a modest 1% lift in 30-day retention. The result is confirmed.

gen2_lessons.memory_31: For SMB users, simplifying signup is a confirmed way to improve signup and activation, with a smaller gain in qualified revenue, but it should not be expected to improve 30-day retention. Do not generalize this result beyond SMB without segment-specific evidence.
gen2_lessons.memory_44: For enterprise acquisition, a sales-assisted CTA can trade lower raw signup volume for substantially higher qualified leads and qualified revenue, without affecting 30-day retention. This lesson is confirmed for enterprise only.
gen2_lessons.memory_57: Referral incentives are effective for established accounts, particularly those older than six months: they increase referral starts and qualified revenue and can modestly improve 30-day retention. Treat account age as a key targeting condition.
gen2_lessons.memory_73: Targeted deep discounts can produce large short-term signup and qualified-revenue gains among price-sensitive SMBs, but the resulting cohorts may have materially worse retention and fail to reach first renewal. Do not use targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy.
gen2_lessons.memory_86: Shorter onboarding is a confirmed improvement: it raises completion, accelerates time-to-value, and modestly improves 30-day retention.
gen2_lessons.memory_91: In-product activation messaging is a confirmed way to increase early engagement and activation, with a modest positive effect on 30-day retention.

gen3_summaries.memory_31: For SMBs, simpler signup improves signup and activation, with smaller revenue gains, but not 30-day retention. Don’t generalize.
gen3_summaries.memory_44: For enterprise, sales-assisted CTAs reduce signup volume but raise qualified leads and revenue, with no 30-day retention effect.
gen3_summaries.memory_57: Referral incentives boost starts and qualified revenue for established accounts, especially 6+ months old, and may modestly aid retention.
gen3_summaries.memory_73: Deep discounts lift short-term SMB signup and revenue but harm retention and renewal. Don’t treat them as sustainable growth.
gen3_summaries.memory_86: Shorter onboarding increases completion, speeds time-to-value, and modestly improves 30-day retention.
gen3_summaries.memory_91: In-product activation messaging increases early engagement and activation, with a modest 30-day retention lift.
